description.narrative:
Maternal & child health: Increase access to integrated basic health services for women, babies, and young children
Adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights (ASRHR): Improve capacity among adolescents to make informed decisions about their SRHR
Children & Adolescents living with HIV: Evidence based psychosocial support models for improving health outcomes among adolescents living with HIV developed
Gender based violence: Reduce gender-based violence amongst adolescents
Child marriage: Reduce incidents of child marriage

REPSSI has ansökt om stöd från Sida med ett totalt belopp om 45 miljoner kronor vilket utgör kärnstöd för REPSSIs strategiska plan 2016-2020. Stödet avser att täcka tre år (2016-2018) av den totala fem-åriga strategiska planen. Stödet syftar till att förbättra det psykosociala och mentala välbefinnandet bland pojkar, flickor och unga personer i 13 länder i östra och södra Afrika; Angola, Botswana, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Sydafrika, Swaziland, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia och Zimbabwe.
Följande övergripande mål gäller för REPSSI verksamhet: (i) Förbättrad kapacitet bland ungdomar att ta informerade beslut relaterade till SRHR (ii) ökat behov och användande av SRHR tjänster bland ungdomar (iii) ökat antal personer som genomgår och fullföljer behandling bland barn, ungdomar och unga som lever med HIV (iv) utvecklandet av evidensbaserade metoder för psykosocialt stöd för förbättrad hälsa bland ungdomar som lever med HIV (v) minskning av könsbaserat våld bland ungdomar (vii) minskat antal barnäktenskap. Den regionala ansatsen väntas generera synergieffekter i from av metodutveckling, erfarenhetsutbyte och påverkan på regionala policy och regelverk.
Den totala budgeten för REPSSIs strategiska plan under femårsperioden är uppskattningsvis 202,600.000 kronor. Sidas bidrag kommer att svara mot ca 35% av den årliga budgeten under de första tre åren. Ytterligare en ca 25% kommer att anslås från av Schweiz genom SDC. Comic Relief och USAID har utlovat runt 10.000.000 (5%) i projektfinansiering för 2016 medan REPSSIs eget bidrag som utgörs av internt mobiliserade resurser är beräknas utgöra 6% av budgeten. Medan 2016 är fullt finaniserat så arbetar REPSSI med att mobilisera ytterligare finansiering för kommande år.

REPSSI has submitted a funding application of SEK 45 000 000 to Sida as a contribution towards REPSSI's 2016-2020 Strategic Implementation Plan. The overall goal of the intervention is the improved psychosocial and mental well-being of girls, boys and youth in East and Southern Africa.
Aligned to this goal are the following expected outcomes (i) Improved capacity among adolescents to make informed decisions about their SRHR; (ii) Increased demand and use of SRHR services by adolescents; (iii) Increased initiation, retention on treatment for children, adolescents and youth who are living with HIV; (iv) Evidence based psychosocial support models for improving health outcomes among adolescents living with HIV developed; (v) Reduced gender-based violence amongst adolescents; and (vii) Reduced incidence of child marriage. REPSSI's regional approach generates synergies through methods development, experience sharing and policy advocacy at regional level.
The total budget for REPSSI's Strategic Implementation Plan is approximately SEK 202,600.000 for the five-year period. Sida's contribution will cover approximately 35% of the annual budget for the first three years. Additional funding of approximately 25% will be provided by Switzerland through SDC. Comic Relief and USAID have committed about SEK 10 000 000 (5%) in project financing for 2016 while REPSSI's own mobilised resources cover approximately 6% of the budget. While 2016 is fully financed, REPSSI is mobilising additional resources for the coming years.

REPSSI provided technical support and led advocacy initiatives to mainstream psychosocial support (PSS) in programmes and services for girls, boys, youth, families, and communities in East and Southern Africa. Mainstreaming PSS in social, health and education programmes and services was premised on the understanding that PSS helps children, adolescents, youth and their families and caregivers gain confidence in themselves, enhances their coping skills and improves decision making on SRH and HIV issues.
REPSSI conducted and trained partners to facilitate community dialogues, training and implementation of initiatives linked to the objectives. Through engagements with community members, health practitioners, adolescents, youth and community stakeholders, more than 10 million girls, boys, and youth were reached through all project areas through 68 different partnerships.
Examples of achievements as highlighted in the "End Phase Report" (conducted by REPSSI) include:
- Officially establishing the Africa Psychosocial Support Institute (APSSI) as a functional subsidiary of REPSSI to serve as a hub for academic research, PSS knowledge development and dissemination.
- Strengthening of regional partnerships with SADC and the EAC, including continuing domestication of the SADC Minimum Package of Services and the EAC Minimum Standards, in collaboration with national governments in all countries in which REPSSI is operational. This led to greater appreciation of, and demand for, PSS. A study to track budgeting for PSS showed that many governments in the region have included PSS in policies and programmes, and some are budgeting for PSS;
- Continued advocacy to end child marriages in seven countries with the highest levels of child marriage in the region, and extended advocacy and communication relationships with media across all countries;
- Developed a campaign to encourage adolescents and youth to be tested for HIV.
- Held a successful PSS Forum in Tanzania in 2017 that brought together over 400 international delegates; including media from the 13 countries where REPSSI works, who were further sensitised on PSS appropriate reporting in addition to their coverage of the forum. This year witnessed increased PSS social and behaviour change communication messaging, enabling REPSSI to reach many in different languages via a variety of media.
- REPSSI became more active, visible and influential in a number of national and regional Technical Working Groups;
- Engaged in webinars, training and establishment of a regional Community of Practice on Mental Health and PSS in humanitarian emergencies in East and Southern Africa.
The intervention exceeded the initial targets set for several areas, including for the ending child marriage campaign where a target was set of reaching 500 000, but the results almost doubled to 965 564 people. Another example relates to the 'HIV testing in children and adolescents campaign', which reached 164 859, exceeding the target of 100 000. The programme also exceeded its targets in terms of resource mobilisation where a target of 4 new funding sources was set, but the programme gained 21 new funding sources.
